name: Crawford Art Gallery
watch: National Cultural Institution of Ireland located in Cork.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2010 to 2024 and financial statements 2016 to 2024, lists ten board members, and names three partners with other funders by logo.

name: Cubitt
funding: Arts Council England NPO, Islington Council, Outset Contemporary Art Fund, artist studio rents. Registered Charity No. 1049602.

name: CUE Art Foundation
funding: National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), NYSCA, NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, private philanthropic grants. 501(c)(3) public non-profit.
watch: Dedicated to creating opportunities for emerging and underrepresented artists of all ages.

name: Dar Jacir for Art and Research
funding: Kickstarter raised nearly $24,000 in 2017. A.M. Qattan Foundation, Sida-funded, announced a $255,691 grant via the Institute for Palestine Studies in March 2018. AFAC lists three grants.
watch: Its owners said Israeli soldiers raided it on 15 May 2021 and took equipment, per Hyperallergic. Emily Jacir and Aline Khoury co-direct it.
records_note: Posts yearly Donors and Partners pages naming supporters, with named text through 2020; no annual reports, accounts or board are published.

name: De La Warr Pavilion
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £518k and Rother District Council £477k core; Esmée Fairbairn, Art Fund, Levelling Up Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund.
records_note: Stakeholder and impact reports run 2018-19 to 2025; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; funders and trustees are named.

name: De Pont
funding: Private museum run by a foundation built on the estate of Jan de Pont.
watch: Established in 1992 by the bequest of jurist and entrepreneur Jan de Pont.
records_note: Its site states the foundation is self-funded and audited, posts a two-year income summary only, lists a five-member board, and names no funders or reports.

name: DK Rozy (Rosa's House of Culture)
watch: Dedicated to working-class education, feminist theory, and anti-war solidarity.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
funding: Public-private partnership of the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation and INTACH. The Corporation paid INR 2.8 crore for the 2025 reopening repairs.
watch: Mumbai's oldest museum; it reopened on 8 January 2025 after four years closed.
records_note: Names its Board of Trustees, chaired by the Mumbai mayor; no annual reports, accounts or donor list are published, only membership tiers.

name: E-WERK Luckenwalde
funding: Kulturstiftung des Bundes, Brandenburg science and culture ministry, Teltow-Fläming district, Mittelbrandenburgische Sparkasse. Kunststrom sales of biomass electricity part-finance the art programme.
watch: Former coal power station now runs on locally sourced biomass. Spanner Re2, a biomass firm, gives support.
records_note: Its site (kunststrom.com) posts no annual report, accounts, funder list or board; the legal notice names only a managing director, Pablo Wendel.

name: Espacio Cultural Patiño
funding: Financed by the Patiño foundations: the Bolivian university foundation Simón I. Patiño created in 1931 and the Geneva foundation his heirs set up in 1958.
watch: Opened 1984; one of three Patiño centres. La Paz bought two neighbouring houses and opened new galleries in 2018; over 35,000 visitors a year.
records_note: No records of its own; the Geneva Fundación Patiño posts activity reports 2022 to 2025 and names its board, with no accounts or donor list.

name: Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam
funding: Small photo museum (193k visitors 2019); City of Amsterdam, tickets, VriendenLoterij, VandenEnde Foundation, Garanti BBVA International (bank), Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation.
watch: A lottery and a bank are the corporate names to know (partnerships page, Dec 2025).
records_note: Annual reports for 2024 and 2025 carry the accounts, named funders and the supervisory board; an undated partnerships page names four major partners.

name: Fondation Vincent van Gogh Arles
funding: Set up in 2010 after Luc Hoffmann backed it. Maja Hoffmann, a Roche heir, chairs the board, which includes the Mayor of Arles. Partners: Hiscox, Blackwall Green, Christie's.
watch: Roche is a pharmaceutical group, no flag category. Maja Hoffmann also chairs the LUMA Foundation behind LUMA Arles.
records_note: Names its institutional partners, corporate partners and sponsors on a partners page and lists its board of directors; no annual reports or accounts are posted.
